title: Diagnosing Epistemic Uncertainty in Neural Operators: Effects of Initialization, Discretization, and Function Sampling
abstract: arXiv:2611.31526v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for mappings between function spaces, but their reliability cannot be characterized by the performance of a single trained model. Existing neural operator uncertainty quantification approaches often characterize predictive uncertainty without separately identifying the contributions of individual sources of epistemic uncertainty. Finite sampling of the training function space, output discretization, and model initialization can produce substantial variation among learned operators even when the underlying physical problem is deterministic. We systematically investigate these sources of epistemic uncertainty across a diverse set of operator learning architectures. Across our experiments, we train approximately 46,000 neural operator models and construct ensembles over training datasets, model initializations, and output discretizations to characterize distributions of relative $L_2$ error rath

translated_title: 诊断神经算子中的认知不确定性：初始化、离散化与函数采样的影响
translated_abstract: 神经算子为函数空间之间的映射提供了高效的代理模型，但其可靠性无法通过单一训练模型的性能来刻画。现有的神经算子不确定性量化方法通常只刻画预测不确定性，而未能分别识别认知不确定性各来源的独立贡献。即使底层物理问题是确定性的，训练函数空间的有限采样、输出离散化和模型初始化也会在所学到的算子之间产生显著差异。我们在多样化的算子学习架构集合上系统地研究了这些认知不确定性来源。在实验中，我们训练了约46,000个神经算子模型，并在训练数据集、模型初始化和输出离散化上构建集成，以刻画相对L2误差的分布特征。
tldr: 该论文系统研究了神经算子中认知不确定性的三大来源（训练函数采样、输出离散化、模型初始化），通过训练约46,000个模型并构建集成，定量刻画了各来源对算子学习性能差异的独立贡献。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically investigates three sources of epistemic uncertainty in neural operators—function sampling, output discretization, and model initialization—by training approximately 46,000 models and constructing ensembles to quantify the independent contributions of each source to performance variation.
